blocks.text: 质量间隙指向一个谜题。在方程中，胶子没有质量，而由无质量粒子传递的力通常会延伸到很远。由无质量的光传递的电磁力就是一个例子。相比之下，强相互作用力只在极短距离内起作用，例如在原子核内部。物理学家对此的解释是，胶子聚集成确实具有质量的结构，而且其中即使最轻的也不是无质量的。零与该最小可能质量之间的间隙被称为质量间隙。计算机模拟支持这一点，但还没有人从数学上证明它。

blocks.text: The computer science result centers on the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH). It concerns the Boolean satisfiability problem, or SAT. SAT deals with a logical formula whose variables can only be true or false. The question is whether you can set the variables so the whole formula comes out true.

blocks.text: With only a few variables, you can just try every combination. But each new variable doubles the number of possibilities. With 100 variables, you're already looking at a 31-digit number.

blocks.text: Put simply, the ETH says there's no real shortcut. You can speed up the trial and error, but in the worst case, computing time still grows exponentially, increasing by a fixed factor with every added variable.

blocks.text: The mass gap points to a puzzle. In the equations, gluons have no mass, and forces carried by massless particles normally reach very far. The electromagnetic force, which massless light carries, is one example. The strong force, by contrast, only acts over tiny distances, such as inside an atomic nucleus. Physicists explain this by saying gluons clump into structures that do have mass, and even the lightest of them isn't massless. The gap between zero and that smallest possible mass is called the mass gap. Computer simulations support it, but nobody has proven it mathematically.
